name: Read the Sealed Shelf
gloss: One mind held open to every colleague in the hall; one mind held shut against every eye outside it. Neither alone builds a library — the first without the second is gossip, the second without the first is a locked box nobody can use. Together they are a shelf that is both fully public and fully secret: different walls of the same room, never one mind's work.

roles.gloss: The reader. She holds the room's knowledge open to every colleague who asks, which is the half of the working that makes the shelf usable at all.
The warden. He holds the room's knowledge shut against everyone who is not a colleague, which is the half of the working that makes the shelf worth keeping.

effects.gloss: The whole faculty reads faster while the shelf stands open to it — a bonus neither caster's own track produces at this scale by itself.
The same shelf gives nothing to a raider who was never granted the room. No single mind, however well warded, keeps a secret this deep alone.

name: Found the Hollow Hall
gloss: A hall raised over a chamber that was never filled in. The mason's line does not teach where a floor may safely be left hollow; the sapper's does not teach how to raise a course of stone above one. This working has exactly two authors — it rises faster than either doctrine manages alone, because the mason spends no effort fighting ground the sapper already left alone on purpose.

roles.gloss: The mason. She raises the stone that becomes the hall, holding the only doctrine in the grid that still trusts a wall to stay up.
The sapper. He opens the exact chamber the hall is built over, holding the only doctrine that knows precisely where the ground will give.

effects.gloss: Construction across the whole university moves at a pace neither doctrine reaches alone — the mason is never waiting on ground the sapper has not already cleared.
The hollow beneath the hall is not waste; it is stock, drawn out clean because the sapper never has to fight the mason's own foundations to reach it.
